announced.basis: documents this watch saw appear between one run and the next. Everything present when the watch was seeded is deliberately absent here: it was already known and was never new.

as_of_means: The date of the last live crawl, not today. This feed goes visibly out of date rather than silently.

awaiting_minutes.basis: an agenda posted for a past date whose file id has no minutes alongside it in the town's listing. This is minutes against AGENDAS, not against meetings held -- the same proxy sources/data/minutes-coverage.csv rests on, and the town publishes nothing that reconciles the two.

first_seen_means: The day our crawler first saw a document. The town publishes no posting timestamp, so a gap between a meeting and its minutes appearing is an UPPER BOUND on how long the town took, never a measurement of it. Documents adopted when the watch was seeded have no first_seen and are excluded from every lag figure.
not_a_measurement: This file records what the Lunenburg Budget Project's crawler could see on the town's AgendaCenter on the date given. It is not a figure checked against a document, and it must not be presented beside one as the same kind of number.

recent.basis: one row per meeting from sources/data/meeting-register.csv -- the one record a meeting has -- for past meetings the town posted or published something about in the window; every artifact we hold for it is on the row. Newest activity first.

our_minutes.headline: Finance Committee skeptical of funding the special ed reserve with free cash before a use policy exists; Collins review scope sent back.
Conservation Commission approved the Lake Shirley boat ramp rebuild with wetland buffer waivers.
Committee voted to hire Rich Matthew as director of finance and operations, pending contract; requested $300,000 free cash for special ed reserve.
Commission approved several septic and other compliance certificates and two NOIs, and continued most hearings to October 21.
Board set Lunenburg Middle High gym as Nov 3 polling place and put several articles on the Nov 17 warrant.
Commission voted unanimously to support the food pantry's variance for modular units, and to seek a joint meeting on the Brooks House.
Committee agreed it is too early for a November warrant article and kept shaping a square-footage-and-cost RFP package.
Parks Commission reviewed the beach season and field fees; fee and Wallace Court lighting decisions were put off to the next meeting.
Assessors voted to put two veterans-exemption articles, clauses 22I and 22J, on the November 17 town meeting warrant.
Sewer Commission discussed raising the late-payment interest rate and demand fee to match nearby towns; no vote was taken.
Planning Board approved both 10 Parmenter Road phases and 149 Summer Street; the 30 School Street food pantry hearing was continued to October 19.
Cemetery Commission approved August minutes, reviewed the back-lot expansion bid timing, and moved its maintenance rules toward a separate policy.
Committee agreed to draft a scope of work for a town-hall architect, using an estimated 63–8,400 sq ft need; next meeting Oct 5.
The committee voted to restore a second-grade teacher and literacy funding over an audit or a second BCBA.
The school committee voted to submit its own warrant article demanding the full extra state aid for the September 3rd special town meeting.
Commission tabled extending Town Beach hours after fee revenue fell short of what the May increase was expected to bring in
Select Board approved FY26 budget amendments; deferred action after a newly surfaced Fitchburg water billing shortfall
Select Board voted 3-2 to pull the APDC/Historical Commission merger article from the special town meeting warrant
Select Board delays votes on the APDC-historical commission merger and a new noise ordinance amid pushback
Select Board voted most fall Special Town Meeting warrant articles, including a new special-education reserve fund
Select Board approved a charity bike ride's route through town, then entered executive session for litigation.
Select Board terminated Flat Hill Road contractor for cause; school's ~$582K FY25 surplus remains unverified
Select Board finalized the town meeting warrant, including a roughly $49M budget and a citizen override question.
Board put most town meeting warrant articles on the warrant; override and school supplement deferred to next night.
The town is racing to fund a citizens petition restoring cut sports and transportation before the August 27 hearing.
Select Board interviewed three town manager finalists; no vote or selection was made at this meeting.
School Committee unanimously approved a new director of finance and operations title and hired a temporary director.
Select Board advanced the Food Pantry's temporary move to 30 School Street, waiving fees and OK'ing a license.
Planning Board approved flood-plain and multi-dwelling special permits for three properties; two hearings continued for lack of quorum.
Select Board again declined to call a special election on the FY26 school override town meeting had approved.
Select Board reviewed a $13.7M Marshall Park rebuild going to the May 3 town meeting as a debt-exclusion vote.
Select Board voted not to put the schools' override question on the town election ballot, ending it.
Sewer Commission voted to seek a combined multi-year pump station O&M/construction contract for Nov. town meeting
Board designated the middle-high school cafeteria as polling place and ratified a new fire chief and police officer.
Commission voted to redesign the Cowry Nature Center ADA trail route to avoid direct wetland alteration.
Commission ratified an emergency order clearing a blocked culvert that flooded a Lancaster Ave home.
Commission to seek Town Meeting authority to set its own wetlands permit fee schedule, vote due mid-September

upcoming.basis: an agenda posted for a date on or after as_of. An agenda is not a guarantee the meeting happens, and a meeting can be held with no agenda posted.
